title: Eight utility READMEs ship hv's absolute home path into an install
body:
Eight `opt/*/README.md` carry a literal `/Users/matts/Devel/prj/Utilz`, two occurrences each, in a "Development" section pointing at where to edit the source:

```
1. Edit `/Users/matts/Devel/prj/Utilz/opt/stampz/stampz`
4. Update help if needed: `/Users/matts/Devel/prj/Utilz/help/stampz.md`
```

`cryptz`, `clipz`, `expz`, `gitz`, `macoz`, `mdagg`, `retry`, `stampz`. The other seven READMEs are clean.

**Found by ST0014/WP-05's end-to-end, not by reading.** READMEs are in the install's owned set, so a published install carries hv's home directory path in eight files. It is inert -- **zero CODE files in the owned set name any absolute home path**, which is what makes the install relocatable and is pinned by a test -- but it is someone's home directory shipping inside a distributable tree.

**THE ORIGINAL DIAGNOSIS WAS WRONG, AND CORRECTING IT IS THE MOST USEFUL THING IN THIS RECORD.** This issue said the generator "is NOT the cause and does not need changing", and that the fix was "a one-time edit of eight files and not a code change". That was read off `tmpl/README.tmpl`, which does ship the literal string `$UTILZ_HOME` at lines 19 and 53-56 -- but the Development section is not written that way. It uses `{{IMPL_PATH}}` and `{{HELP_PATH}}`, and `common.sh` filled those with ABSOLUTE paths. **Measured 2026-09-08** by generating a utility into a sandbox: the ninth README came out carrying the sandbox's own absolute path. Fixing the eight files alone would have fixed nothing durable -- the next `utilz generate` would have minted the defect again, and the tenth after that.

**ROOT CAUSE: ONE VARIABLE DOING TWO JOBS.** `impl_path` and `help_path` were both the filesystem target the generator writes THROUGH and the string substituted INTO README.md. Nothing could be made right for the reader without breaking the writer, and the first attempt at this fix proved it: making them relative broke generation outright, reddening `version_dispatch.bats` AT08 with `opt/zzgen31654/zzgen31654: No such file or directory`. Split into an absolute pair (write + operator output) and an `_rel` pair (the README).

**A NOTE ON HOW THAT WAS NEARLY MISSED TWICE.** The sandbox check that first "confirmed" the relative form was run from inside the sandbox, so the relative path resolved against cwd and produced a green that said nothing about the real invocation. The full estate caught it. A path check run from a convenient cwd is not a check.

**RESOLVED 2026-09-08.** Generator split; the eight READMEs edited, 16 occurrences to 0; and `install_e2e.bats` dropped its `! -name '*.md'` exemption, so the strict property now covers the WHOLE owned set instead of only files that run -- which is where the leak actually was. Two controls proved the widened test can fail: an injected home path in a README reddens it, and removing the `/Users/you/` documentation placeholder trips the non-vacuity check. Full estate 576 ok / 0 not ok across 19 suites.

**The original's warning about exception lists stands and was honoured.** The eight were not added to one. What the widened test filters is the `/Users/you/` placeholder, which is a convention available to any document rather than a per-file list, and it is held by a control that fails the moment it stops covering anything real.
